title: Display mouse location and windows clipboard manager not working after switching 'ctrl' and 'alt'
author: zeyugao

status.label: Known remapping limitation
status.detail: A maintainer documented why the clipboard shortcut changes from Ctrl+V to Alt+V and why Mouse Utilities cannot see the released source Ctrl. The clipboard workaround is already known.

next_action: Do not propose a competing Keyboard Manager fix; retain the documented Alt+V-to-Ctrl+V workaround and treat the Mouse Utilities behavior as a separate design limitation.

judgment.rationale: The two reported effects are explained by the configured Ctrl/Alt remapping and an explicitly documented cross-module limitation, rather than an unexplored failure in the current remap path. The clipboard flyout sends Ctrl+V, which becomes Alt+V under this mapping; the maintainer supplied an Alt+V-to-Ctrl+V workaround. Mouse Utilities cannot react to the logical Ctrl because Keyboard Manager releases the original key after pressing the remapped key.
evidence: The report is from PowerToys 0.37.1 and says the clipboard flyout opens but does not paste after Ctrl and Alt are switched; the left Ctrl mouse indicator also fails.
A Keyboard Manager maintainer explained that the clipboard flyout uses Ctrl+V and recommended an additional Alt+V-to-Ctrl+V shortcut remap.
The same maintainer explained that the mouse indicator cannot respond to the logical remapped Ctrl under the current design because the original key is released after the remapped key is pressed.
A 2024 comment still reports the clipboard symptom on v0.85.1, but does not contradict the documented remapping behavior.
judgment.recommended_action: Do not open a code-fix design from this report. Keep the documented clipboard workaround available and consider the Mouse Utilities limitation separately if maintainers want to support logical remapped-key activation.

fix_assessment.rationale: The clipboard result follows from the user's Ctrl-to-Alt remap and already has a specific workaround; the mouse-indicator behavior is a known cross-module design limitation, not evidence of a current remapping defect.

issue_context.summary: Switching Ctrl and Alt reportedly prevents the Mouse Utilities Ctrl-click indicator from activating for the remapped key and makes the Windows clipboard flyout's paste action ineffective.
known_information: The original report lists PowerToys 0.37.1, running as administrator, and says left Ctrl is remapped while right Ctrl still activates the mouse indicator.
The reporter says Win+V opens the clipboard flyout but selecting an item does not paste.
A maintainer explained that the flyout sends Ctrl+V, which the remap turns into Alt+V, and suggested adding an Alt+V-to-Ctrl+V shortcut remap.
A maintainer also explained that Mouse Utilities cannot observe the remapped logical Ctrl because Keyboard Manager releases the original key after pressing the remapped key.
A 2024 commenter reported the clipboard symptom on v0.85.1.
issue_context.analysis: The clipboard symptom is an expected consequence of remapping the modifier used by the flyout, and the maintainer has already supplied a targeted workaround. The Mouse Utilities symptom is a documented limitation of how the current cross-module design exposes remapped key state. The public discussion does not establish a separate regression or a concrete low-risk code change.
initial_investigation: Read the live issue body and all three comments, including the maintainer's explanation and the later v0.85.1 report.
Checked the issue's current metadata and direct PR-reference search; no covering fix or linked PR was found.
